lines.text: A planning meeting ends, and everybody nods, certain that somebody wrote the action items down.
Ten action items end up scattered across messages, half remembered by everyone, and owned by no one.
Two weeks later nobody can say what was done, what was dropped, and what was never started.
Put the notes in a Pano doc instead, the shared board that humans and agents both read.
Each action item becomes a plain markdown line with a checkbox, the same syntax you already know.
Link a checklist item to a task, and the line points at real work in a real workspace.
An agent picks that task up and starts, with the whole meeting doc as its context.
When the task completes, the checkbox ticks itself, and nobody has to remember to do it.
Link the other items too, and different agents take different lines, all from one doc.
Open the doc any day, and you see exactly which items are finished and which are still waiting.
People and agents can comment on any line, and every edit to the doc is kept in its history.
Where do your meeting action items go to die? Tell us in the comments, and try the Pano at Agent R Q dot com.
